```{python}
#| include: false
import os

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# Published by the publish_metrics task, only after the quality checks pass.
bm = pd.read_csv(f'{os.getenv("AIRFLOW_HOME")}/data/behaviour_metrics.csv')

# One series per chart, so one colour; text stays in neutral greys.
BLUE = "#2a78d6"
INK = "#52514e"
GRID = "#e8e7e3"


def show(fig, x_title, y_title):
    """Apply the shared style and display the chart.

    Quarto displays the value of every expression in a cell, so chart code
    assigns each update to `fig` and only this function shows it, once.
    """
    fig = fig.update_traces(marker_color=BLUE)
    fig = fig.update_layout(
        template="plotly_white",
        font=dict(color=INK, size=13),
        margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
        xaxis_title=x_title,
        yaxis_title=y_title,
        barcornerradius=4,
        showlegend=False,
    )
    fig = fig.update_xaxes(gridcolor=GRID, zeroline=False)
    fig = fig.update_yaxes(gridcolor=GRID, zeroline=False)
    fig.show()
```

## Row

```{python}
#| title: Customers by net spend (£)
# Returns can exceed purchases, so some customers have a negative net spend.
buckets = [
    ("Below 0", float("-inf"), 0),
    ("0-500", 0, 500),
    ("500-1k", 500, 1_000),
    ("1k-2.5k", 1_000, 2_500),
    ("2.5k-5k", 2_500, 5_000),
    ("5k-10k", 5_000, 10_000),
    ("10k+", 10_000, float("inf")),
]
dist = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "bucket": [name for name, _, _ in buckets],
        "customers": [
            int(((bm["amount_spent"] >= lo) & (bm["amount_spent"] < hi)).sum())
            for _, lo, hi in buckets
        ],
    }
)
fig = px.bar(dist, x="bucket", y="customers", text="customers")
fig = fig.update_traces(
    textposition="outside",
    cliponaxis=False,
    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y} customers<extra></extra>",
)
fig = fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, dist["customers"].max() * 1.15])
show(fig, "Net spend (£)", "Customers")
```

```{python}
#| title: Top 10 customers by net spend (£)
top = bm.nlargest(10, "amount_spent").assign(
    customer=lambda df: df["customer_id"].astype(str),
    label=lambda df: df["amount_spent"].map("£{:,.0f}".format),
)
fig = px.bar(top, x="amount_spent", y="customer", orientation="h", text="label")
fig = fig.update_traces(
    textposition="outside",
    textfont_size=12,
    constraintext="none",
    cliponaxis=False,
    width=0.6,
    hovertemplate="Customer %{y}: £%{x:,.0f}<extra></extra>",
)
# dtick=1: label every customer, never every other one.
fig = fig.update_yaxes(
    categoryorder="total ascending", type="category", dtick=1
)
fig = fig.update_xaxes(range=[0, top["amount_spent"].max() * 1.25])
show(fig, "Net spend (£)", "Customer")
```

## Row

```{python}
#| title: Net spend vs share of positive reviews
# Log scale because spend is very skewed (median about £1.5k, top £279k);
# a log axis cannot show spend <= 0, so those customers are left out here.
pos = bm[bm["amount_spent"] > 0].assign(
    positive_share=lambda df: df["num_positive_reviews"] / df["num_reviews"]
)
fig = px.scatter(
    pos,
    x="amount_spent",
    y="positive_share",
    log_x=True,
    opacity=0.6,
    custom_data=["customer_id", "num_positive_reviews", "num_reviews"],
)
fig = fig.update_traces(
    marker=dict(size=8, line=dict(width=1, color="white")),
    hovertemplate=(
        "Customer %{customdata[0]}<br>Net spend £%{x:,.0f}<br>"
        "%{customdata[1]} of %{customdata[2]} reviews positive"
        "<extra></extra>"
    ),
)
fig = fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".0%")
fig = fig.update_xaxes(
    tickvals=[10, 100, 1_000, 10_000, 100_000],
    ticktext=["£10", "£100", "£1k", "£10k", "£100k"],
)
show(fig, "Net spend (£, log scale)", "Positive reviews")
```

::: {.card title="How to read this chart"}
Each dot is one customer with a positive net spend
(`{python} f"{len(pos):,}"` of `{python} f"{len(bm):,}"`). The dots form a
flat band: spend and the share of positive reviews are not related
(correlation `{python} f"{pos['amount_spent'].corr(pos['positive_share']):.2f}"`).
That is expected here: a review counts as positive when its text contains the
word "good", and the reviews are linked to customers by id only for this demo.
:::
